newsitem.title: KENYA: U.N. agency wants full access to refugees in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency wants full access to refugees in Zaire.

text.p: U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata urged warring factions on Monday to give aid workers access to hundreds of thousands of exhausted refugees fleeing civil war in the jungles of eastern Zaire.
Ogata expressed hope the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) would keep promises not to attack the Ubundu area where most refugees had converged.

"The refugees are at the end of their strength. Their harrowing odyssey through the wilderness has to stop now, or many more lives will be lost," Ogata said in a statement faxed to Reuters in Nairobi from UNHCR headquarters in Geneva.

The UNHCR would expand its relief operation and start repatriating refugees to Rwanda as soon as it had unimpeded access, but: "They must gather some strength before we can repatriate them to Rwanda," she added.
But Zairean rebels said they were not in control of Ubundu and could therefore not guarantee any access to the refugees.

"We cannot allow the UNHCR to go to a place where we are not in control. If they want to go (to Ubundu) then they will have to deal with those criminals who control the camp," said rebel foreign affairs commissar Bizima Karaha.
Karaha's "criminals" referred to hardline Hutu refugees, accused by Rwanda of involvement in the 1994 genocide of Tutsis and Hutu moderates which slaughtered around 800,000 people.
Ogata said movement of refugees into the jungle west of Ubundu would cause more deaths and make it logistically impossible for the UNHCR to assist them.
"They should stay where they are now since this is the last place where we can locate them and help them," she added.

UNHCR said up to 100,000 refugees were massed on the eastern side of the Zaire river across from Ubundu and thousands more were somewhere between Ubundu and the former refugee camp at Tingi Tingi, about 200 km (125 miles) southeast of Kisangani.

The refugee agency warned that military activities in Ubundu could trigger panic among the refugees, pushing them across the Zaire river and into further wilderness. It warned that a number of people had already drowned while trying to cross the river.
The ADFL rebels led by Laurent Kabila have now overrun about a fifth of Zaire. They captured Kisangani, Zaire's strategic and third largest city, at the weekend.
In Nairobi, the U.N. food aid agency WFP said it was ready to move into Ubundu where refugees had no food as soon as it received "necessary clearances and security assurances".

WFP spokeswoman Michelle Quintaglie told Reuters that one of its warehouses in Kisangani was completely looted while a second had some food but WFP was still taking an inventory. She said other agencies also reported looted warehouses.
She added: "Recent reports indicate that all food in Ubundu has been distributed to refugees, meaning there is no food...I hope we can get back there as soon as possible."
Relief workers started repatriating Rwandan Hutu refugees from Zaire's Tingi Tingi camp but said prospects for those who fled in front of the relentless rebel advance looked bleak.
Some 15 sick Hutu children who have lost their families were the first refugees to be lifted out for repatriation to Rwanda.

The children, aged between six months and 14 years, were flown from Tingi Tingi in a U.N. plane. Some were too weak to walk while others had shrunken limbs and protruding ribs. They will stay in Goma until strong enough to return to Rwanda.
"Only the worst cases, the unaccompanied children and handicapped can be flown out," UNHCR spokesman Paul Stromberg told Reuters in Goma. "Other means will have to be found to bring out the rest."
